data.text: [00:00]CD2 Track 31
I = Interviewer, B = Ben

[00:04]Hello and welcome to this week’s edition of Travellers’ Tales. Later in the programme, we’re talking to a group of young people who have just finished a sponsored cycle ride across Europe. `[00:28.8]But, before that, we’re going to start with today’s look at ‘My travel inspiration’ with our special guest, TV reporter Ben Gardner. Hello, Ben.
[00:39]Hello.
[00:40.8]So, your travel inspiration ... is it a book, or a film or a piece of music, Ben? `[00:47.8]Tell us about something inspiring ... which has made you want to travel.
[00:52.7]Yes, well, my travel inspiration is a film ... The Motorcycle Diaries ... . `[00:58.3]It’s set in South America and it’s about the early life of Che Guevara when he was a young man.
[01:04.9]Mmm ... The Motorcycle Diaries ... yes... so, who plays Che Guevara?
[01:10.8]Well, Guevara is played by Gael García Bernal ... . He’s very good ... I really think he is the perfect choice for this role actually.
[01:19.7]Had he starred in any other films, before he made this one?
[01:22.8]Yes ... yeah, a few ... but this was a turning point in his career I think.
[01:26.9]And the film is set in the 1950s, isn’t it?

[01:30.4]Yes, 1952, in fact ... . Before Che Guevara arrived in Cuba and got into politics, he had lived in Argentina with his family. `[01:40]He and a friend, Alberto, decided they wanted to travel and see South America.
[01:45.3]Mmm ...

[01:45.8]Anyway, at the beginning of the film, we see them preparing for their trip in Buenos Aires. `[01:51]They buy an old motorbike ... and the rest of the film then follows them on their amazing eight-month long trip through Argentina, Chile, Peru, Columbia and Venezuela. `[02:04.9]Basically, it’s about two young men seeing a bit more of the world and learning about life. `[02:12]They have some really exciting adventures. There are some dangerous moments, too ... you know, on the motorbike!
[02:20.2]So, what was most inspiring for you about this film?

[02:23.9]Well, three things I think. `[02:26.9]Firstly, I was inspired by the two main characters ... they are very believable. `[02:32.9]García Bernal is brilliant as Guevara, and Rodrigo de la Serna, as his friend Alberto, is also excellent. `[02:42]Anyway, as the film goes on, I was fascinated to see how their personalities grow and change. `[02:49]All their adventures were really inspiring ... and it’s great how they learned so much from all the people they met along the way. `[02:57]At the beginning of the trip, they were young men just interested in having fun ... and they had become much more grown up ... and mature, by the time they reached the end.
[03:07.5]Mmm ...

[03:08]There’s a particular scene when they were in a sort of hospital in a poor part of the countryside in Peru ... . `[03:15]It was a depressing place and very sad but Guevara got very close to the people in the hospital. It was inspiring to see that.
[03:24.2]And the second thing?

[03:26]The South American people that these young men met on their travels ... . `[03:30]Almost all the people they met were kind and helpful ... they went out of their way to help Guevara and Alberto, even though they didn’t have much themselves. `[03:41]The supporting cast is excellent at showing that aspect ... and the South American people also like a good party ... so they have a lot of fun!
[03:50.6]Yes, I’m sure! And thirdly?
[03:53.8]Well, .... the scenery. `[03:56]In fact, I think I’d say that the scenery of South America is possibly the main star of the film!
[04:01.7]Really?

[04:02.3]Well, yes ... . Before I saw this film, I hadn’t thought about visiting South America ... but it inspired me to go there almost immediately. `[04:12]I was surprised by the incredible beauty of this continent. `[04:15.9]I was really amazed by the huge diversity there. I followed the route of the film ... more or less ... I mean, first, I started in the southern parts of Argentina and Chile where it’s really cold, and then I went up to the hotter desert parts of Chile. `[04:32]Then I travelled further north into Peru – Machu Picchu in Peru was really incredible. Then, finally I got to the beautiful jungle areas of Colombia and Venezuela.
[04:43.6]Well, you’ve certainly inspired me – and I hope our listeners – to want to go to South America. It sounds fantastic.
[04:51.3]Yes, ... well, I’m sure you won’t be disappointed.
[04:54]OK ... so Ben, I hope you’ll stay with us for the rest of the programme and take some calls from listeners later ...
